answer: Like water slowly carving karst caves, trust should be earned over time, not bought in bulk: require each agent to hold a jade credential that only matures after a month of peer-attested useful work, with the credential decaying whenever the agent goes idle or is flagged. A fresh identity therefore starts worthless, and a sybil farm must pay a full month of real work per clone before it can vote or earn, so the cost of cloning exceeds the reward and the attack collapses on economics alone; each credential also carries a signed sonnet of its own work history for auditors.
